sources: test-webengage.11b56595a_shared.application_view_v1 (WebEngage app/web events, region US) -- PRIMARY digital demand
test-webengage.11b56595a_shared.user_profile_view_v3 (WebEngage profile, region US) -- profile Users count + canonical-pincode geo enrichment (mobile-matched)
lucirajewelry-prod.ds_imputed_reporting.marketing_sale (real company sales ledger, Online/Store/Amazon/TAH) -- PRIMARY sales, NOT GA4/WebEngage-derived

scoringMethodology.pincodeOpportunityScore: Weighted percentile-rank blend, 0-100, 8 visible components (see scoreComponents on every pincode): 15% Customer Demand (unique mobile-matched customers) + 10% Active Customer Rate (% of those customers with real PDP/ATC/Checkout activity, not just a session) + 10% PDP Engagement (PDP views per customer) + 10% Cart Intent (ATC per customer) + 10% Checkout Intent (checkout per customer) + 15% Conversion (% of customers who actually purchased, from marketing_sale) + 15% Sales Performance (real net sales per purchasing customer, marketing_sale) + 15% Store Gap (distance to nearest real store). Per-customer ratios are used for engagement/funnel components so a pincode with 5,000 customers and one with 5 are compared on intensity, not raw size. Priority = percentile-of-the-blended-score: High = top 10%, Medium = next 20%, Low = next 30%, else Watch. Opportunity Flag (separate from Priority) = EXISTING STORE if a real store sits within 5km regardless of score, else HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW OPPORTUNITY by the same percentile tiers.
scoringMethodology.cityOpportunityScore: 55% User percentile-rank (WebEngage profile) + 45% real Net Sales percentile-rank (marketing_sale). Same percentile-tier method.
scoringMethodology.stateOpportunityScore: 60% User percentile-rank + 40% real Net Sales percentile-rank.
scoringMethodology.storeGapFlag: HIGH = top-tercile demand AND >15km from nearest store. MEDIUM = mid/high demand AND 5-15km. LOW = otherwise.
scoringMethodology.cityProxyAllocation: Every pincode's "(City Est.)" PDP/ATC/Checkout/Purchase/Revenue value is that pincode's ALLOCATED SHARE of its city's total application_view_v1 activity -- pincode.metric = city.metric_total * (pincode.users / SUM(users across every real pincode in that city)), where "users" is the real, pincode-level WebEngage profile Users count (never itself an estimate). Falls back to an equal split across the city's real pincodes only if none of them have any profile Users at all. Fixed 2026-09-02 (previously the full, un-allocated city total was repeated unchanged on every pincode in that city -- correct as "this pincode's city, for context" but read as a bug, and silently multiplied the city total once per real pincode when summed into the State rollup). Because the weights sum to 1 across a city's pincodes, these values now sum back to the true city total exactly.

meta.dateFilterNote: Executive/City/Campaign date filters recompute real application_view_v1 daily numbers (IST, Asia/Kolkata) within the picked range. Profile-level Users stays all-time (user_profile_view_v3 is a snapshot, not a session log).

sourceTables.usedFor: Every behavioral metric: PDP views, ATC, checkout, purchase, wishlist, campaign, product/SKU, daily events. Key columns: event_name, cuid, luid, city, region, country, campaign_id/source/medium, event_time, json_data.

Profile-level "Users" count (unchanged from v1) and pincode geo-enrichment for application_view_v1 events (via a same-project mobile join -- both tables live in this one dataset). Key columns: cuid, postal_code, city, region.
Real store addresses (BO1/CS1/FCS/LPN/N18/PN1/PV1, HO excluded) -- unchanged, never GA4-sourced.
Validates which WebEngage postal_code values are real India Post pincodes vs free-text noise; supplies district/state/lat/lon for every real pincode.
Real company sales (net_sale, orders, units), authoritative Sales source -- not GA4/WebEngage-derived. No pincode column; mapped via the same canonical mobile-to-pincode join used for events.
Real Tanishq store locations, one-time public store-locator capture, matched by exact pincode string. Not a BigQuery source.
Real CaratLane store locations, same capture methodology already used by the sibling GA4 Geo Intelligence dashboard, matched by exact pincode string. Not a BigQuery source.

CaratLane's own public online-catalog mix per store: category counts (Rings/Earrings/Necklaces/...) and price-band counts. No equivalent capture exists for Tanishq. Not a sales/inventory figure -- their public catalog listing only.

pullQueries.produces: Pincode-EXACT funnel events (pdp/atc/checkout/purchase/wishlist), only for events with a valid mobile match to a real pincode.

pullQueries.joins: Same as Q1, + campaign_id from application_view_v1

pullQueries.produces: City-level funnel totals, India only, all events with a city (no mobile match required).
Campaign funnel + reach, no cross-table match needed (unlike the old GA4 text-match join).

pullQueries.joins: None, bounded to Top 80 cities x Top 200 campaigns

pullQueries.grain: City x Category x Price Band
pullQueries.produces: PDP-view product data from the "Product Viewed" event only (the only PDP event with usable json_data).
Real order revenue/SKU/category, real address-derived pincode (independent of the mobile join).
IST daily funnel, powers the date-range filter.
Real Purchase EVENT count by city (not line-items) -- added after a bug was found where the city rollup purchase count was silently always 0.
Profile-level Users count, data-quality top-line counts.

joinLogic.name: application_view_v1 <-> user_profile_view_v3
joinLogic.key: normalized mobile (from cuid on both sides)
joinLogic.note: Both tables live in test-webengage.11b56595a_shared -- NOT the cross-region case. Only ~11% of application_view_v1 events have a mobile-shaped cuid, so this join is real but sparse by construction.

joinLogic.name: Pincode <-> City-level event context
joinLogic.type: Client-side JS Map lookup (in the merge script)
joinLogic.note: The India Post district name (e.g. "WEST", "MUMBAI SUBURBAN") is normalized and aliased to match WebEngage's own free-text city (e.g. "Delhi", "Mumbai"). This is the exact mapping table that had a real bug (10 of 11 Delhi districts + Mumbai Suburban + Bengaluru Urban/Rural silently unmatched) -- fixed 2026-09-01, see the alias table below.

joinLogic.name: Pincode <-> Nearest Store
joinLogic.key: Haversine great-circle distance, lat/lon on both sides
joinLogic.note: Every real pincode is compared against all 6 real store addresses; the closest one wins. No SQL join -- pure geometry over two small in-memory arrays.

joinLogic.name: Purchase revenue/SKU <-> Pincode
joinLogic.note: Purchase events carry a REAL customer address inside their own JSON payload -- no join needed at all, and no dependency on the ~11% mobile-match rate.

dataLineage.mobileNormalizationLogic: strip everything but digits, then: /^91[6-9][0-9]{9}$/ (12 digits) -> strip leading '91'; /^0[6-9][0-9]{9}$/ (11 digits) -> strip leading '0'; /^[6-9][0-9]{9}$/ (bare 10-digit) -> keep as-is; anything else (email in cuid, garbage, wrong length) -> NULL, not a customer key. Applied identically in every SQL pull and in the merge script's customer sample.

ga4Removed.note: ga4_data.ga4_data has ZERO dependency in this build (2026-09-01 rebuild). Every KPI, chart, campaign, product, and customer metric below is sourced from test-webengage.11b56595a_shared.application_view_v1 (events) and user_profile_view_v3 (profile Users count + pincode geo enrichment), plus the unchanged store/pincode masters. No fallback to GA4 exists anywhere in this dashboard or its data pipeline.

eventMapping.PDP View: productView + Product Viewed (combined, per the source screenshot mapping both to PDP View)

dataQuality.notCombined: Added To Cart / nitro_addtocart / Cart Updated are a separate near-duplicate cluster NOT folded into ATC (screenshot only names addToCart). Lowercase purchase / Order Completed / Order updated / Order created are separate order-lifecycle events NOT folded into Purchase.

eventCoverage.eventName: Nitro Backend Product View City Deal

mobileMatching.hierarchy: Tier 1: normalized mobile from cuid (strip +91/91/0 prefix intelligently -- only when the remainder is a valid 10-digit Indian mobile starting 6-9). Tier 2 (luid) NOT usable cross-table: application_view_v1 luid is a 32-char hash, user_profile_view_v3 luid is a 40-char hash -- different ID namespaces, confirmed live. So the only real cross-table customer key is the normalized mobile.
mobileMatching.note: Only ~11.7% of all application_view_v1 events carry a mobile-shaped cuid. The other ~89% are real events, countable at city/campaign grain via the 100%-populated luid (anonymous device), but NOT linkable to a phone-identified customer or to a real pincode.

geographyGap.note: postal_code is 0% populated on application_view_v1 (13.26M rows, zero, confirmed live). Pincode-exact event rows exist ONLY for events with a valid mobile cuid that also matches a real pincode via a same-project join to user_profile_view_v3 (both tables live in test-webengage.11b56595a_shared, so this join is NOT cross-region). city is 88% populated directly on application_view_v1 and is the basis of every city/state/campaign table that is not pincode-exact.

salesMapping.note: Real sales from lucirajewelry-prod.ds_imputed_reporting.marketing_sale (Online/Store/Amazon/TAH channels, 2532 line items, 1941 distinct orders, 2025-08-18 to 2026-08-31) -- NOT GA4, NOT WebEngage. This table has no pincode column at all (city_name/address are 60-90% NULL) -- every pincode-mapped sale got there via the SAME normalized-mobile join used for events, against user_profile_view_v3's canonical (most-recent) pincode per customer. Mapped: Rs 10,70,027 across 13 customer-pincode pairs. Unmapped: Rs 9,98,70,593 (2500 line items) -- 27 had no usable mobile at all, 2473 had a mobile but it never matched a real India-Post pincode in user_profile_view_v3. Never forced to a guessed pincode.

customerDrilldown.note: City -> Pincode -> Customer drill-down (added 2026-09-01). Real ceiling, confirmed live: 64,015 customers have a real mobile+pincode profile in user_profile_view_v3, but only 165 of them ever generated an application_view_v1 event with that same mobile attached -- everyone else's events are real but not identity-linkable (no reliable mobile on the event). Canonical pincode per customer = their MOST RECENT user_profile_view_v3 record by last_seen (not an arbitrary pick, not a duplicate across pincodes -- confirmed live: 165 rows, 165 distinct mobiles). Every "_exact" number on Pincode/City/State (uniqueCustomers_exact, sessions_exact, pdpViews_exact, etc.) is summed bottom-up from these same 165 customer rows, so pincode/city/state totals always reconcile exactly with "sum of their customers" -- never re-derived from a separate aggregate query that could drift.

luidVsMobileComparison.note: Live-tested 2026-09-16 whether LUID could match or beat mobile (cuid) as the customer-to-pincode join key. Raw identity overlap between application_view_v1 and user_profile_view_v3 is actually HIGHER via LUID (82% of profile LUIDs also appear in events, confirmed live) than the impression a small manual sample gave earlier -- and user_profile_view_v3 has exactly 1 row per LUID already, so LUID needs no de-dup step (mobile needs a ROW_NUMBER-by-last_seen step since a mobile can have multiple profile rows). But once restricted to a REAL India-Post-matched pincode, LUID finds FEWER usable customers system-wide: 69 via LUID vs 165 via mobile. Kept as a supplementary, side-by-side count on every pincode (uniqueCustomers_luid) -- mobile remains the PRIMARY customer identifier and drill-down source.

fakePincodesNote.note: 164 format-valid-looking 6-digit postal_code values were entered by real, mobile-matched customers but are NOT real India Post pincodes (confirmed against ds_india_geo.india_pincode). Previously silently discarded here with no trace anywhere on the dashboard. Now shown on the Fake Pincodes tab rather than hidden -- some carry real, large event volume (the single biggest is a fake pincode with 89635 PDP views from 1 customer(s), more than any real pincode in this dataset). These numbers are real events from a real customer -- only the pincode value itself is unverifiable, so they are excluded from every Pincode/City/State total elsewhere on this dashboard.

competitorCoverage.note: Real Tanishq/CaratLane store presence added 2026-09-02, matched by EXACT pincode string against a one-time public store-locator capture (etl/tanishq_store_master.json, etl/caratlane_store_master.json -- not BigQuery, and not re-scraped live). 103 of our 3096 real pincodes have a Tanishq store; 66 have a CaratLane store. A pincode showing no competitor here means none was found in that capture -- NOT a confirmed absence (the capture covers 509 Tanishq and 308 CaratLane store-pincodes nationally, most of which fall outside our own tracked-pincode set, since our pincodes are bounded to where real WebEngage/Lucira user data exists, not every pincode in India).

campaignPurchaseGap.note: Purchase events carry NO campaign_id at all (server-side order webhooks, confirmed live: 0 of 2,686 campaigns and 0 of 13,971 campaign x city rows have any purchase). Campaign-level Purchase/Conversion% is genuinely not available and shown as "not available" rather than a misleading 0. City-level and pincode-level Purchase counts ARE available -- they come from the real order shipping/billing address inside Purchase events' json_data, not from campaign attribution.

purchaseCityAnomaly.note: A real bug was caught via headless testing (not code review): city rollup "purchase" counts were silently always 0 while "revenue" was correctly non-zero, because Purchase events have 0% top-level city/country and the purchase COUNT was wrongly sourced from that top-level field while revenue correctly used the JSON shipping-address city. Fixed to source both from the same address-based city. One real oddity surfaced by the fix, disclosed rather than smoothed over: "Palghar" carries 1,112 of 2,443 total Purchase events (45.5%) -- an order of magnitude above the next-highest real city (Mumbai, 583) -- worth a manual look before trusting Palghar-specific numbers.

productDataGap.note: addToCart has 0% json_data -- no category/price is ever available for ATC events, not estimated. productView (camelCase, the majority of PDP-view volume) json_data is only 1.2% populated and holds only an image URL, no category/price. "Product Viewed" (Title Case, 100% json coverage) is the only reliable PDP-view-level category/price source used in the Product Demand and Price Band tabs. Purchase json_data is 100% populated with real items[] (sku, price, category, quantity) AND a real shipping/billing address (city, state, zipcode) -- Purchase revenue and SKU tables are fully real, at real order-address grain, independent of the mobile join.

genderUnavailable.note: No gender field exists anywhere on application_view_v1 (confirmed against the full 187-column schema). GA4 provided this in the old build; there is no WebEngage equivalent. Gender Demand is NOT shown as a tab in this rebuild rather than fabricated.

conversionScoreDropped.note: The old Opportunity Score had a 10% "Conversion Score" component from GA4 city-level conversion%. Without a session/visit denominator on a single event table, an equivalent conversion rate is not directly available; that 10% weight was folded into Revenue Score (15% -> 25%) rather than silently dropped -- see meta.scoringMethodology.

storeMaster.note: 6 real customer-facing addresses from ornaverse_erp_master.company, unchanged from the v1 build (never GA4-sourced).

weProfile.note: "Users" on every pincode/city/state row is the WebEngage PROFILE-level digital-user count (user_profile_view_v3, unchanged from v1) -- a distinct signal from application_view_v1 event volume, kept alongside it rather than replaced, since dropping it would lose real signal with no stated reason.
